solutions.task: Write a Python function to validate AWS S3 bucket names. A valid S3 bucket name must be 3-63 characters long, contain only lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens, and periods, start and end with a letter or number, and cannot contain consecutive periods or hyphens at the start/end.
solutions.solution:
import re

def validate_s3_bucket_name(bucket_name: str) -> bool:
    if not isinstance(bucket_name, str):
        return False
    
    if len(bucket_name) < 3 or len(bucket_name) > 63:
        return False
    
    if not re.match(r'^[a-z0-9]', bucket_name):
        return False
    
    if not re.match(r'[a-z0-9]$', bucket_name):
        return False
    
    if '..' in bucket_name:
        return False
    
    if bucket_name.startswith('-') or bucket_name.endswith('-'):
        return False
    
    if not re.match(r'^[a-z0-9.-]+$', bucket_name):
        return False
    
    return True


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_cases = [
        ("my-bucket", True),
        ("my.bucket", True),
        ("mybucket123", True),
        ("a", False),
        ("ab", False),
        ("abc", True),
        ("my-bucket-", False),
        ("-my-bucket", False),
        ("my..bucket", False),
        ("my_bucket", False),
        ("MY-BUCKET", False),
        ("my-bucket" + "x" * 60, False),
        ("my-bucket.test", True),
        ("1bucket", True),
        ("bucket1", True),
    ]
    
    for bucket_name, expected in test_cases:
        result = validate_s3_bucket_name(bucket_name)
        status = "PASS" if result == expected else "FAIL"
        print(f"{status}: {bucket_name} -> {result} (expected {expected})")
